findings.title: التهاب السحايا يهدد أطفال غزة.. 15 وفاة و272 إصابة خلال تشرين الأول
findings.publisher: WAFA Palestinian News and Information Agency
findings.location: Nasser Medical Complex, Khan Younis; Al-Rantisi Children's Hospital, Gaza City; Gaza Strip
findings.affected_population_system: New firsthand reporting documents a displaced mother saying she was instructed to leave Nasser Medical Complex with her child with meningitis on the third day because more severe cases needed care and infection risk was high. Medical Relief director Dr Mohammed Abu Afash reports severe shortages of laboratory testing supplies across medical points. The report also states Nasser received over 500 cases (period not specified) and Al-Rantisi recorded about 145 cases, 15 bacterial, during September 25–October 25. These are facility-level reported figures, not new incidence this hour; overlap with overall surveillance counts is unknown.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: وفي اليوم الثالث أبلغتني إدارة المستشفى بضرورة مغادرتي، نظرا لوجود حالات أكثر خطورة من حالة طفلي
findings.source_type: Established news agency; named firsthand patient-family interviews and named medical relief official

bounded_discovery_context.method: Direct Arabic WAFA home page health/report section and full dated article, compared with the November 24 WAFA surveillance report and Al Jazeera report; 13 prior authenticated heartbeat files read (five recent, eight earlier).
bounded_discovery_context.novelty: Publication at 15:16 local (05:16 PST) is within the observation window. Specific bedside account of hospital capacity-driven discharge and facility counts add to the earlier surveillance figures and alert, which are not counted again.
bounded_discovery_context.caveat: Mother's testimony and facility counts not independently corroborated; no specific discharge date, clinical disposition assessment or period for Nasser total verified. Publication offset inferred. Do not sum facility figures or treat earlier 272 cases, 15 deaths, 100 November bacterial cases or genotyping limitations as new.
